title: Enforce onboard contract + stability probation and add changelog-qualifier annotation
author: Leah Martinez
description:
Context: Model onboarding has increasingly become a source of silent regressions when variants are accepted into the registry without a clear machine-enforced contract and without an intermediate stability window. Operators and integrators need two guarantees: (1) Onboard metadata must follow a minimal contract so automated tooling (release assembler, profiling pipelines) can rely on specific fields; (2) Newly onboarded variants should be marked as 'probation' for a configurable period so changelog generation and rollout automation can treat them conservatively.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds an onboarding contract validator (jsonschema) that runs as a pre-commit/pre-submit check in the onboarder service and as a CI gate for registry PRs.
- Introduces metadata fields: "probation_until" (ISO date string) and "probation_reason" (short tag). If present and in the future, the variant is considered probationed.
- Enforces probation semantics in the registry API: probationed variants are excluded from automatic promotion and flagged in the query API, and they now surface a stability_score reduction for downstream tooling.
- Extends the changelog generator to emit a "(probation)" qualifier on release notes entries for any variant whose probation_until is not expired. This makes changelogs explicit about stability.
- Adds a small migration that backfills probation_until for variants with no observed evaluation history (30-day probation default) and leaves older, vetted variants untouched.

Checklist (implemented):
- [x] JSON schema for onboard contract (required fields: name, arch, family, baseline_metrics, quantization_profile, compatibility_tags)
- [x] Registry acceptance rule that rejects onboard artifacts failing the schema (with clear error messages)
- [x] DB migration + backfill tool and a dry-run flag for ops
- [x] Changelog generator hook to append "(probation)" and to add a stability footnote in release blobs
- [x] Unit tests for validator, probation rule, and changelog qualifier
- [x] E2E integration test using the local onboarding harness

Testing and validation notes: The validator is covered by 24 unit tests (schema permutations), the probation behavior has 6 integration tests that simulate onboard -> query -> changelog flow, and we ran the backfill in dry-run mode against staging (approx 1.2k variants scanned). CI: all checks passed after two iterative fixes to error messages (see conversation).

Migration and rollout plan: Deploy validator as a soft-fail feature flag for 48 hours (only warn, do not block), then flip to enforce. Run backfill in parallel (dry-run first, then commit-window). After sufficient telemetry showing few rejections, enable probation-aware promotion rules. Ops playbook included in docs (link: ./docs/onboard-probation.md).

Backward compatibility: Existing variants without probation fields continue to be treated as production-stable unless backfill sets probation_until. The validator includes a compatibility whitelist for legacy imports.

Performance impact: The validator is designed to be cheap (schema check only); changelog qualification adds negligible latency to release assembly (<5ms per variant). DB migration runs as a batched job to limit spike.

Related: ENG-4211 (onboard hardening), ENG-4299 (rollout safety), SUP-1082 (customer reported variant confusion).

release_notes: Introduce an onboarding contract validator and a temporary 'probation' metadata flag. New variants may be auto-tagged as probationed and will show a '(probation)' qualifier in changelogs until the probation period expires or they are manually promoted. Includes DB migration and backfill; soft rollout controlled by feature flag.
